text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Israeli embassies: Israel's image deteriorating because of the deadlock in peace talks.
- Reserve air force brigadier general suspected of having known that price of Panther helicopter was inflated by $10 million.
- Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan: "Thousands of Jordanian workers have asked to work in Israel, but applications were not accepted."
- Israeli Border Police soldier suspected of beating Palestinian, threatening his life if he filed complaint against him.
- Contrary to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's statement, treasury to recommend cutting defence budget.
- Naamat women's organisation: Authorities to demand that thousands of adopted youths born abroad undergo "rigorous conversion" to Judaism in order to marry.
- World Jewish Congress is negotiating with Swiss banks on establishing foundation to aid survivors of Nazi holocaust.
JERUSALEM POST
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon: Israel's security cabinet "in the dark" about (emerging agreement on troop withdrawal from) Hebron.
- Palestinian Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo warns of violence if current Israeli policy continues.
- Israeli Transportation Minister Yitzhak Levy relearns the rules of the road.
- Syria would accept U.S.-led summit with Israel, U.S. Senator Arlen Specter says.
- Israeli army: budget cut won't reduce military strength.
MAARIV
- Defence official warns: if defence budget not enlarged, there will be more deaths in the next war.
- China sold Iran materials for producing nerve gas - Washington Times.

- If asked by local authorities in Hebron-area Jewish settlement, Army's Central Front commander will approve moving grave of Baruch Goldstein from Kiryat Arba. Goldstein massacred dozens of Arabs in Hebron mosque in 1994.
- Palestinians: Israeli policy could bring about a total confrontation.
- Religious Jewish burial officials fence off grave of woman in section of cemetery reserved for "Sabbath observers" because her family suspected of having owned a television.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel intends to establish three new settlements on the Golan Heights.
- Senior doctors recorded explaining how to act "as though treating" terminal patients.

- The Soldiers' Welfare Association forgave $1.3 million loan to David Agmon, director-general of prime minister's office, "for humanitarian reasons", before Agmon was appointed to post in prime minister's office.
GLOBES
- Yitzhak Kaul to be named head of Clal.
- IDB Holdings Chairman Rafael Recanati: "A Great Wall of China is being built, entirely separating Clal and Discount Investments".
- Avi Patir turns down Communications Minister Limor Livnat's proposal to head Bezek.
